uncoveredCases: Flask-AppBuilder @expose/@action route variables are matched as handler function parameters (excluding self); FAB's internal URL routing/converters are not modeled, so a <string:dag_id> row does not carry the converter type (no <path:...> converter exists outside serve_logs.py's /log/<path:filename>).

connexion (REST API v1) does not read the flask request object for path/query parameters: they arrive as handler kwargs driven by openapi/v1.yaml. All functions defined under airflow.api_connexion.endpoints are treated as handlers (their non-parameter helpers included); the OpenAPI spec itself is YAML and outside CodeQL python analysis.

request aliasing: the www_request parameter of get_date_time_num_runs_dag_runs_form_data (airflow/www/views.py:205-225) is matched by name as a request alias; other local aliases of flask request would be missed (no flow-sensitive alias resolution at extraction time).

DB-derived path fields (DagModel.fileloc, TaskInstance dag_id/task_id/run_id, LogTemplate filename) are attacker-influenced only through DAG authorship and are NOT extracted as sources (no DB taint source in a path-traversal pass without an established boundary); the handlers that pass them into file APIs appear as sinks/internal wrappers instead.

importlib.machinery.SourceFileLoader(...).exec_module (dagbag.py:341, plugins_manager.py:254) executes a file by path; it is extracted as a sink family, but the exec_module() method call itself is not separately modeled.

Dynamic/aliased file wrappers: correct_maybe_zipped returns a transformed path (redirect node, not extracted); file wrappers reached only through kwargs indirection (e.g. set_file_paths programmatic injection, dag_processor_command args.subdir default from settings.DAGS_FOLDER) rely on the wrapper/param families rather than per-hop dataflow.

Providers' remote filesystem hooks (sftp/ftp/gcs/s3 local-to-remote copies, e.g. providers/sftp/operators/sftp.py Path usage) are covered by the generic open/Path/os/shutil families, but remote-path arguments of hook APIs (hook.get/put) are not a distinct family - only local filesystem operations are in scope for CWE-22 on this pass.

No multipart write-to-disk exists: request.files appears once (varimport) and the uploaded filename is never used in a path; FileStorage/secure_filename/.save() do not occur - so the upload-filename source family is intentionally empty (not fabricated).
No archive extraction exists (no extract/extractall anywhere), so no Zip-Slip sink family is emitted; ZipFile(...).open member reads are matched by the .open method family.
